Charles McPherson has been one of the top alto saxophonists in jazz since the 1960s. He was born in Joplin, Missouri on July 24, 1939 and moved to New York City at the age of 20. One of his first gigs was with bassist Charles Mingus, and this fruitful relationship lasted until 1974. While his playing reflects the influences of Johnny Hodges and Charlie Parker, he has developed a distinctive character on the alto that has in turn influenced numerous younger saxophone artists. Charles has recorded frequently throughout his career, often with pianist Barry Harris. He has led his own ensembles since 1972 and can be heard with his son Chuck on drums. Author Stanley Crouch sums up the deep sense of purpose he brings to his music in the liner notes to “First Flight Out.”
Crouch states, “McPherson never lets us forget the actual greatness of the art he represents.”
Charles was interviewed in San Diego, California on February 12, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
